experiments.title: Can the model recognize exposed water?
experiments.plain_result: Water mapped by the model overlapped the reference much better in August (97%) than October (41%). The August model had limited value on the later scene.
experiments.scope: Fitted on 246,399 August cells with NISAR HH and HV. Tested on separate areas in August and the same withheld areas in October. A clear optical image supplied the exposed-water reference.
notes: Overlap is intersection over union. These measurements address exposed water in this one floodplain. For under-canopy flooding or drought, use independent evidence.
The October and paired tests used the August-fitted model without retuning.

experiments.title: Can the model identify a reported slick?
experiments.plain_result: The oil screen evaluated 172 of 46,942 cells in the independent slick outline and flagged 0 inside it. Quality checks left most of the outline unevaluable.
experiments.scope: Calibrated on NISAR HH measurements off Oman. Held the settings fixed for the reported GEM NO. 2 spill near Umm Al Quwain.

metrics.label: Reference cells with a matching flag

notes: The reference outline was mapped about 39 minutes after the NISAR pass. A public incident report confirms the spill. Wind, waves, timing and signal quality affect this screen.
The offshore map marker is a location to inspect visually. The screening method issued no match inside the eligible reference cells.

experiments.title: Does a second channel help in the marsh?
experiments.plain_result: At Shark River Slough, adding HV information raised overlap with the modeled marsh water reference from 66% to 83%. The test covered one date in this marsh.
experiments.scope: NISAR HH and HV on 27 October, grouped into 400 m cells. Spatial testing used 2,813 cells. The radar quality rules withheld 1,604 of the 4,417 depth and habitat reference cells.
notes: EDEN estimates depth between water-level gauges. The original test used 0 cm versus at least 10 cm in mapped freshwater emergent wetlands.
This site-specific test uses different labels and a coarser analysis grid than Curuai.

experiments.title: Could the river screen evaluate the inspection area?
experiments.plain_result: The river screen evaluated 246 nearby water cells and identified no connected dark patch. The inspection area itself fell outside the usable part of that screen.
experiments.scope: Compared 24 February and 8 March NISAR HH around the OEFA inspection location, using 60 m analysis cells and a 40 m exclusion near river banks.
notes: OEFA documented the incident in the field. Its inspection area gives a location and has no simultaneous slick outline for scoring radar detections.
The displayed 20 m change layer compares the measured radar return. The detection screen used a separate coarser grid and stricter quality conditions.

experiments.title: How much of NOAA’s outline was also dark in NISAR?
experiments.plain_result: At Eugene Island, the trial flagged darker water in 362 of 1,730 cells within the NOAA outline. NISAR measured this scene 43 minutes earlier.
experiments.scope: A cutoff fitted on Oman HH was frozen before testing new Louisiana sites. The trial compares the measured HH echo with nearby water and has no per-pixel noise layer for the strict oil test.

metrics.label: Eugene Island cells flagged outside the outline, material unknown

notes: Solid red marks recorded dark water inside the near-time NOAA outline. The dashed red boundary is NOAA’s separate possible-oil observation.

experiments.title: Can the Curuai model transfer to a salt lagoon?
experiments.plain_result: The same wetland screen withheld all Atanasovsko cells. The background radar noise was too close to the brightness cutoff used to find water.
experiments.scope: Used the fixed August Curuai rule on a new site and date. The nearby optical observation arrived 16 hours after NISAR.

notes: Dashed orange traces the independent optical water reference. This trial gives no estimate of radar detection accuracy at the lake.

evidence.title: USGS · EDEN regional water depth estimates
evidence.notes: EDEN combines gauge observations, spatial interpolation and ground elevations. The marsh benchmark uses the resulting modeled water depths.
